text:
customer-acme: hey @support, since 08:03 our prod instances in the on-prem VPC are seeing huge latency and intermittent 403s against the Redwood API. We're in us-west but our requests are landing in EU; adds ~400ms. started after a maintenance window this morning.

jessica (support): sorry to hear that — can you paste a quick curl + traceroute and confirm your egress topology (NAT/peering/TGW)?

customer-acme: topology = onprem -> customer-hub (peering) -> hub-nat -> cloud-peering -> redwood private endpoint. here's quick curl we ran: 
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/ping -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n"
* Connected to api.redwood.com (52.50.16.12) port 443 (#0)\n> GET /v1/ping HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood.com\n> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK\nX-Region: eu\n...\n200 0.422
```

samir (support): can you run these and paste outputs?
1) `traceroute api.redwood.com`
2) `tcpdump -nni any 'host api.redwood.com and port 443' -c 3`
3) `curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.com/v1/ping -o /dev/null -w '%{remote_ip} %{time_total}\n'`

customer-acme: traceroute: 
```
traceroute to api.redwood.com (52.50.16.12), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  hub-peering (198.51.100.2)  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.0 ms
 3  hub-egress (35.178.22.10)  5.2 ms  5.1 ms  5.1 ms
 4  52.50.16.12 (52.50.16.12)  420.6 ms  421.0 ms  420.9 ms
```

and tcpdump shows source IP rewriting to 35.178.22.10 (hub-egress) when hitting api.redwood.com.

mike (eng-infra): reading that output: hub-egress IP (35.178.22.10) geolocates to EU. looks like your hub NAT SNATs internal srcs to the hub egress address. Redwood routes requests to region based on source IP — that's why you hit our EU edge and see the X-Region: eu header, which also explains the auth hiccups (tenant keys are regional-scoped in our private routing).

jessica (support): we also see intermittent 403s in our logs with X-Region: eu for that tenant. here's a small log snippet: 
```
2026-03-12T08:05:12Z tenant=acme req_id=... endpoint=/v1/generate src_ip=35.178.22.10 region=eu status=403 note="key-region-mismatch"
```

customer-acme: correct — the hub NAT was put in as a quick fix to avoid asymmetric return paths (hairpin issues). It was changed during the maintenance window.

mike (eng-infra): root cause summary: hub is SNATing to an egress IP that is announced/peered out of EU side due to BGP localpref on the hub. Because the source IP is EU, Redwood's edge selection routes to EU, causing cross-region latency and tenant auth mismatch.

kyla (eng-oncall): suggested remediations (short and long):
- short: we can enable a region-hint override for tenant acme so our routers prefer us-west despite source IP (temporary, non-invasive).
- short-cust: change hub NAT to preserve source (avoid SNAT) or use a specific SNAT IP that's geo-located to us-west. e.g. `iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.0.0.0/16 -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source <usw-egress-ip>`
- long: fix hub BGP policy to prefer us-west for Redwood prefixes (adjust localpref or community).

samir (support): can you try the diagnostics below then?
1) remove SNAT temporarily (if safe) and retry `curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.com/v1/ping -o /dev/null -w '%{remote_ip} %{time_total}\n'`
2) if removal not possible, add static SNAT using a us-west egress IP as Mike suggested.

support-bot: Ticket SUP-2026-3421 created and linked to this thread.

customer-acme: we disabled hub SNAT for the internal subnet and retried:
```
$ curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.com/v1/ping -o /dev/null -w "%{remote_ip} %{time_total}\n"
203.0.113.45 0.042
```
no X-Region header, latency down to ~42ms, no 403s.

jessica (support): great — marking this as customer-verified fix. we'll keep the ticket open for BGP policy follow-up. thanks for the fast turnaround. :tada:

mike (eng-infra): follow-up action: we'll audit hub BGP localpref and schedule a config rollout to ensure redwood prefixes prefer us-west where appropriate. also will add a KB article for customers running hub NAT (hairpin NAT pitfalls + recommended SNAT/static-ip patterns).

customer-acme: thanks everyone, confirmed stable for 30m. closing on our end.

kyla (eng-oncall): :thumbsup: closing the Slack incident but leaving SUP-2026-3421 open until the BGP policy change is in prod and KB published.

support-bot: Thread archived to SUP-2026-3421.
